newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-NEW SIGNING THERN BACKS RANGERS IN EUROPE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NEW SIGNING THERN BACKS RANGERS IN EUROPE.

text.p: Sweden midfielder Jonas Thern officially joined Glasgow Rangers from Roma as a free agent on Tuesday, saying his new club could make a long-overdue impact in the European Cup Champions' League.

The Scottish champions' poor showing in the competition in recent seasons has seen them included in next week's draw for the qualifying round, but Thern expects Rangers to progress much further than that.

"People criticise Scottish football and say it's only about Rangers and Celtic," said the 30-year-old Swede, "but for games in Europe, it does not matter if you play in the strongest league, only that you have a good team.
"That happened with me when I was at Benfica. We got to the later stages of the Champions' League in 1991 even though the Portugese league was not the best.

"However, we had a good team and Rangers have now got many good players and I think the future is good for us. Walter Smith (Rangers' manager) told me the club can do better in the Champions' League and that is what attracted me here."

Thern, who has signed a three-year contract at Ibrox, said he had received six offers since making a verbal agreement with Rangers six months ago under the conditions governing freedom of contract following the Bosman case
"Fiorentina, Bologna, Parma and Internazionale all wanted me to stay in Italy and I had offers from Gothenburg and Helsingborg to go back home," he said.
